header.name: Biomedical Image processing
header.description: The Biomedical image processing course is meant to impart  knowledge on medical and biomolecular imaging.  The course introduces physical, engineering and signal processing principles needed for medical imaging and image processing. The primary focus of this course will be computational image processing methods. This course covers topics on analysis of medical images from different types of sources such as planar x-ray, x-ray computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), nuclear medicine imaging - positron emission tomography (PET), light  and confocal microscopy and electron microscopy. Students will also gain hands on experience with medical image processing software to process CT or MRI scans and construct 3D models from microscopic images.

lecture_topics: Introduction to different kinds of biomedical images and revisiting basic mage processing procedures: Image Filtering, Enhancement, and Restoration: Contrast Enhancement, Bit-Level Slicing, Histogram Equalization, Mask Processing: Linear Filtering in Space Domain, Frequency-Domain Filtering

lecture_topics: Edge Detection and Segmentation of Images: Sobel Edge Detection, Laplacian of Gaussian Edge Detection, Canny Edge Detection, Point Detection, Region Segmentation Using methods like, Luminance Thresholding, Region Growing and Quad-Trees.
Image transforms : DCT, DWT, CWT, STFT
Principles of Computed Tomography:Attenuation Tomography,  Reflection Tomography,Diffraction Tomography,Fourier Slice Theorem

Processing data from cellular and molecular Imaging Techniques, Optical Microscopy, Fluorescent Microscopy, Confocal Microscopy,  Transmission Electron Microscopy, Scanning Electron Microscopy, etc
